/: When recovering a broken system, verify key top-level folders under '/'.
/bin: If shell scripts fail, confirm core binaries like /bin/sh and /bin/ls exist.
/boot: After kernel upgrade, check /boot for new vmlinuz and initrd files.
/dev: To write a USB image, target device files like /dev/sdb carefully.
/etc: Inspect /etc/ssh/sshd_config when SSH settings are wrong.
/home: Backup only /home to preserve user data while reinstalling system packages.
/lib: Use ldd to find missing shared libraries causing app startup errors.
/opt: Place vendor software in /opt to keep package-manager files separate.
/proc: Read /proc/meminfo to troubleshoot high memory usage.
/root: Store emergency maintenance scripts in root's home for admins only.
/sbin: Run fsck from /sbin in maintenance mode to repair filesystems.
/tmp: If app installs fail, check available space and permissions in /tmp.
/usr: Find package-provided executables in /usr/bin and manuals in /usr/share/man.
/var: Investigate outages by reading logs in /var/log.
Monitor /var/lib growth for services like Docker or databases.
